item.title: Lions’ Brian Branch, DJ Wonnum both suffer concussions in heated Vikings showdown
item.description: Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Lions’ Brian Branch, DJ Wonnum both suffer concussions in heated Vikings showdown appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Sunday, the Detroit Lions hit the field at home for a key NFC North showdown against the Minnesota Vikings . The Lions were looking to build off their momentum from last week’s win over the Green Bay Packers and hand the Vikings their first loss of the season in the process. Unfortunately, the Lions didn’t make it through this game unscathed from an injury perspective , as two members of their defense suffered the same injury in this one. “#Lions Injury Update: EDGE DJ Wonnum (Concussion) has been downgraded to Out. DB Brian Branch (Concussion) has been downgraded to Out,” reported the team on its official account on X, formerly Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Earlier in the game, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had been evaluated for a concussion, but thankfully was cleared to return to the game, having suffered his own injury on a play in which a touchdown was wiped from the board after replay review. Meanwhile, Branch only recently returned to the field after missing the first several games of this season, having torn his Achilles down the stretch of last season. If Wonnum and Branch are forced to miss extended time with their concussions, it would certainly be a tough break for a Lions defense that was just starting to round into form this season. In any case, at the conclusion of the Vikings game, the Lions will hit the field next week on the road vs the lowly Miami Dolphins. Kickoff for that game is set for 1:00 pm ET. item.description: "Today has to be the day." That is what manager Mikel Arteta said before Arsenal secured their first Premier League win at Anfield in 14 years, beating Liverpool thanks to Kai Havertz's first-half goal . Arteta was Arsenal captain the last time the Gunners won at Liverpool - 2-0 in 2012 - and they have had 16 unsuccessful trips in all competitions until Sunday's victory. The Spaniard's side, as they so often do, produced a defensive masterclass to keep out wave after wave of Liverpool attack to deliver a rare and historic win. Arsenal travelled to Anfield after an embarrassing loss to League Two Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday. Arteta said he thought that humbling loss in Lancashire could spur his side on to a historic win at Liverpool. "Extremely proud. It's been 14 years, that's a long time," Arteta said after the game. "I'm sure we made everybody attached to the club extremely proud today. Not only for the victory but for the way we've done it, the spirit we've shown. "Especially considering what happened four days ago when you lose and go out of the cup against a team you are supposed to beat. That's the magical part of this game, it can take you to really bad places but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic and we've done it. "Overall, to win against a team that is producing what they are doing, and also in the emotional state after Fleetwood, that's what a winning team should do." Before the match, centre-back Gabriel said that Arsenal were expecting a "big battle" and "big chaos" against Liverpool. That prediction was correct and, after going ahead, Arsenal were pinned back before the break. item.title: Shelton adds former Alcaraz coach Ferrero to team
item.description: Ben Shelton says he's adding former world number one Juan Carlos Ferrero to his coaching team (Hector RETAMAL) Ben Shelton, who reached his first Grand Slam final at the US Open in September, is adding former Carlos Alcaraz mentor Juan Carlos Ferrero to his team, both parties said Sunday. "Huge addition to my team for this upcoming season," Shelton said in an Instagram story featuring a photo of himself and Spain's Ferrero. "Excited to get started ... Let's get it." Shelton, 24, is at a career-high fourth in the world with a career-best four titles in 2026. The American left-hander reached his first major final in New York, beating Alcaraz in a five-set quarter-final but eventually falling to Alexander Zverev in the title match. Shelton has largely been coached by his father, Bryan Shelton, winner of two singles titles in his own ATP playing career. Spain's Ferrero, who guided Alcaraz to his first six Grand Slam titles before their partnership ended last December, said he was looking forward to working with both the elder and younger Sheltons. "Ben has extraordinary talent, power and character," Ferrero said in a statement. "I'm very happy to join Bryan and the team in this exciting new chapter. I'm looking forward to contributing my experience and working together to help Ben achieve his ambitions on the biggest stages." Ben Shelton also emphasized that Ferrero, a former world number one and winner of the 2003 Roland Garros title, would be an addition to the current team, not a replacement. "Juan Carlos is one of the great minds in tennis," Shelton said in a statement. "His experience of winning at the highest level and developing champions will be a huge asset to our team. "My dad has been such an important part of my journey, and I'm excited about what we can all achieve together as we look to the future." bb/js

item.title: Week 8 Game Recap: Buccaneers run game does it again, run-first shutout victory
item.description: Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) hands the ball to running back Bucky Irving (7) against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Coming off of a running bonanza against Carolina for their second win of the season, week eight was set to feature more running, a downpour, and no Baker Mayfield glove. Would a second consecutive game of relentless running by the Buccaneers’ offense be enough for the Buccaneers to climb out of their early season hole and to the top of the NFC South? First Quarter: It was Todd Bowles’ defense up first on Sunday. Battling on a water-logged field, Tampa’s strongest unit took the field and bent a bit, however, there was no break. The Falcons pushed into Tampa territory before ultimately needing to settle for a long field goal attempt. Weather conditions not favoring Nick Folk, the kick was missed and missed badly. Converting turnovers into points or this case missed field goals into points gave Tampa the first lead of the day. 3-0, Buccaneers. The response from the Falcons was quite mild, an interception by Alex Anzalone. Penix looking for Drake London on a slant, found Anzalone for his second interception of the season. Turnovers into points would fail Tampa on their next drive— Bucky Ivring, breaking into space on a broken play, was met by Jessie Bates at the goal line for a 2023 Antoine Winfield Jr.-esque forced fumble stripping the ball out at the goal line which rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Rest assured, Tampa’s defense understood the assignment. Back on the field, following an Alex Anzalone pick that didn’t result into points, fans watched Michael Penix drop back and throw another Alex Anzalone interception— His second of the day and third of the season. One more field goal off of an Alex Anzalone interception and the Buccaneers expanded their lead. 6-0, Tampa Bay. Second Quarter: The difference between the start of the game’s first quarter and its second? Not much. More rain and more Micheal Penix interceptions. For the start of quarter number two, Penix, under pressure from Rueben Bain Jr., decided to spread the wealth tossing a fourth down interception to Jacob Parrish. Back on the field after another turnover, Tampa Bay’s offense stayed consistent. Run, run, run, and run. The Buccaneers’ only pass attempt of the drive would actually wind up as a rush attempt as well after Baker Mayfield scooped up his third fumble of the day and scurried forward for a short gain. Tampa’s first drive of the second quarter ended with 4:04 left in the half and three more points on the scoreboard. 9-0, Buccaneers. The Bucs and Falcons would each exchange run-first, slow-paced, non-scoring drive to close out half number one and head to the intermission— The only first half since 1978 to feature less than three completed passes. Converting turnovers into points or this case missed field goals into points gave Tampa the first lead of the day. 3-0, Buccaneers. The response from the Falcons was quite mild, an interception by Alex Anzalone. Penix looking for Drake London on a slant, found Anzalone for his second interception of the season. Turnovers into points would fail Tampa on their next drive— Bucky Ivring, breaking into space on a broken play, was met by Jessie Bates at the goal line for a 2023 Antoine Winfield Jr.-esque forced fumble stripping the ball out at the goal line which rolled through the end zone for a touchback. Rest assured, Tampa’s defense understood the assignment. Back on the field, following an Alex Anzalone pick that didn’t result into points, fans watched Michael Penix drop back and throw another Alex Anzalone interception— His second of the day and third of the season. One more field goal off of an Alex Anzalone interception and the Buccaneers expanded their lead. 6-0, Tampa Bay. Second Quarter: The difference between the start of the game’s first quarter and its second? Not much. More rain and more Micheal Penix interceptions. For the start of quarter number two, Penix, under pressure from Rueben Bain Jr., decided to spread the wealth tossing a fourth down interception to Jacob Parrish. Back on the field after another turnover, Tampa Bay’s offense stayed consistent. Run, run, run, and run. The Buccaneers’ only pass attempt of the drive would actually wind up as a rush attempt as well after Baker Mayfield scooped up his third fumble of the day and scurried forward for a short gain. Tampa’s first drive of the second quarter ended with 4:04 left in the half and three more points on the scoreboard. 9-0, Buccaneers. The Bucs and Falcons would each exchange run-first, slow-paced, non-scoring drive to close out half number one and head to the intermission— The only first half since 1978 to feature less than three completed passes. Third Quarter: With zero first half completions and a two-score lead, Baker Mayfield was under center at the 30 yard line to start the third quarter— Run, run, third down drop, and a punt. Tampa Bay, still repping their signature no completion streak, sent their defense back out onto the field for another three-and-out stop. The third quarter was nothing but rain and punts until the final five minutes. Bucky Irving ripped through Atlanta’s defense for a 45 yard rush— Two plays later, it was Kenny Gainwell’s turn. Gainwell, with his second break away run in as many weeks, put the Buccaneers inside the 10 yard line. It would be another two plays until Bucky Irving put the Bucs inside the end zone. 16-0, Tampa Bay. Fourth Quarter: The Falcons seized some bits of momentum in the waning moments of the third quarter. With the final quarter beginning at the Tampa Bay 30 yard line and an Atlanta decision. Neglecting a short field goal the Falcons opted for a forth down attempted and converted with a Michael Penix tush push. Unfortunately for Falcons’ fans, the team would ask Penix to throw next and he would once again throw to a Tampa Bay defender. Penix’s fourth interception would be tossed to Zyon McCollum. Atlanta’s next bite at the apple would be from their 12 yard with just over seven minutes to go— Three-and-out. Tampa’s response— Three-and-out. Backed up from their own two, Michael Penix found Atlanta’s biggest spark of the day— Jahan Dotson for 76 yards. Dotson’s catch and run was the only chink Todd Bowles’ armor, the Falcons’ drive was immediately stalled afterwards and the Buccaneers salted away the rest of the clock and the game. Tampa Bay, despite their 0-4 start, is 3-5 and very much in contention of the NFC South.

item.title: Illinois gets two players back for season opener, but Mirkovic suffers another setback
item.description: Illinois basketball will get some much-needed reinforcements for Monday night’s season opener against Fairleigh Dickinson, but the injury news isn’t all positive for the Fighting Illini. Head coach Brad Underwood confirmed Sunday that both Andrej Stojakovic and Zvonimir Ivisic will be active and in the lineup when Illinois opens its regular season at State Farm Center. Both players suffered injuries during Illinois’ exhibition loss to Baylor last month. Stojakovic and Ivisic each took hard falls and appeared to hit their heads, forcing them to leave the game. Neither played in Illinois’ final exhibition against UIC. There was less encouraging news regarding sophomore forward David Mirkovic. Underwood revealed Sunday that Mirkovic underwent an emergency appendectomy Saturday night after developing appendicitis. His appendix was removed, and he will not play Monday. Mirkovic was already recovering from offseason foot surgery that has kept him out of all three exhibition games. The preseason All-American had recently been spotted working out without his walking boot before returning to the boot and scooter during Illinois’ exhibition against Baylor. Underwood did not provide a timetable for Mirkovic’s return. Freshman guard Lincoln Williams also remains questionable for Monday’s opener. Underwood has not provided an indication of whether Williams will be available. Illinois opens its season against Fairleigh Dickinson at 7 p.m. Monday at State Farm Center.

item.description: Andoni Iraola says that he will tell his players to go down in future after Liverpool were denied a penalty in Sunday's defeat by Arsenal. With Liverpool trailing 1-0 after Kai Havertz's opener, Alexander Isak's shirt was pulled by Jurrien Timber in the first half as he went for a header from Bradley Barcola's cross. However, the Liverpool striker stayed on his feet and referee Andy Madley did not point to the spot. Stuart Attwell, on video assistant referee (VAR) duty, determined that there was not enough in the tug for the decision to be overturned, but Iraola disagreed. "There is a clear grab of the shirt," the Spaniard told Match of the Day. "Alex [Isak] was just in front of him, he was going to head in front of the goal but couldn't because he grabbed the shirt. "If he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100%. It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it." On what the answer is going forward, Iraola added: "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it." Isak turned and spoke to Timber after the incident, but did not appeal to the referee after staying on his feet. Iraola told Sky Sports that going forward, managers should tell their players to go to the floor. On if he will tell Isak that going forward, he added: "Yes, definitely." He elaborated in his news conference when asked by BBC Sport if he would have to tell his players to be more smart, going forward. "It's a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them, go down, because they're not going to call it otherwise. And then referees complain why they go down. item.title: Should Brian Fariñas start at right-back for Barcelona against Aston Villa?
item.description: Photo by Alex Caparros - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Hansi Flick was forced into a few creative changes at the back in Satuday’s dominant La Liga win over Alavés, and while Frenkie de Jong’s performance at center-back has been the subject of plenty of attention, Brian Fariñas’ display at right-back cannot be overlooked. The 20-year-old midfielder made his debut for the first team out of position but had a very good night, looking comfortable in the role and making smart contributions in attack with his overlapping runs and passes into the final third. His defense was also solid, and Fariñas is definitely in contention to remain in the lineup for Tuesday’s Champions League clash with Aston Villa at Camp Nou. The status of Jules Kounde remains uncertain as of now and Flick could also go with a more traditional full-back duo of João Cancelo and Alejandro Balde, but Fariñas’ name cannot be discarded. Kai Havertz’s 16th-minute goal proved decisive as the Gunners ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Liverpool’s ground, moving three points clear of Manchester City at the top of the table. But while Havertz will deservedly take the headlines for his winning goal, it was Arsenal’s collective defensive display that particularly impressed the former Manchester United defender. item.title: Michigan drops two spots in ESPN’s SP+ rankings after beating Rutgers
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 31: Wide receiver Salesi Moa #12 of the Michigan Wolverines runs with the ball after a catch chased by Defensive back Devonte Anderson #21 of the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first quarter at SHI Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Mark Smith/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images Michigan once again didn’t turn in a clean performance on Saturday, defeating Rutgers by a 28-21 final score despite being favored by more than two touchdowns. As such, Michigan found itself dropping two spots in the latest edition of ESPN and Bill Connelly’s SP+ rankings, now sitting at No. 29. For those of you who might be new to SP+, it’s an advanced metric that takes into account a team’s offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the “average” college football team by on a neutral field. In other words, it’s a metric designed to look at how “good” teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes. Michigan’s rating is 11.5 after Week 9, meaning that it would beat an “average” college football team by 11.5 points. The Wolverines flipped the script a bit against Rutgers, with their defense having something of a letdown while the offense looked a bit better. Still, SP+ has Michigan’s offense as the No. 87-ranked nationally and the defense as the No. 4-ranked nationally. The Wolverines still have four games left on their schedule this season, with three of their opponents — Oregon, UCLA, and Ohio State — all ranked higher. That means that Michigan would be predicted to finish the regular season at 6-6. Looking ahead to next week, Michigan will square off against a 2-6 Michigan State team in the Battle for the Paul Bunyan Trophy. Michigan will be going for its fifth straight victory over its in-state rival, which ranks as the No. 85 team in SP+ with a rating of -3.1. That means that the Wolverines are predicted to win by about two touchdowns and will get the advantage of playing on their home field as well. We’ll see how things pan out when the teams take the field at 7:30 p.m. at the Big House on Saturday.

item.title: Sensational playmaker who plays like Philippe Coutinho is coming to Liverpool
item.description: Sensational playmaker who plays like Philippe Coutinho is coming to Liverpool Liverpool have agreed a deal and have secured their new Philippe Coutinho in the process. The Brazilian was simply a sensation footballer. His Liverpool exit left a bitter taste there is no denying that, but looking back, it's difficult to begrudge him for that decision. The money the Reds received from Barcelona also helped fund the arrivals of Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker, so it's fair to say Liverpool got a pretty good deal out of it. Barcelona, perhaps, not so much. Still, with a bit of hindsight, you can really appreciate just how special Coutinho was. The Brazilian was an absolute magician, a natural no.10 who made the game look effortless. He could glide past defenders, pick a pass that nobody else saw and unlock even the tightest of defences. His vision and technical ability were right up there with the best, and he always seemed to know exactly where his teammates were. When Coutinho was at his best, there weren't many players who could match the kind of creativity and magic he brought to the pitch. Florian Wirtz is struggling to be Liverpool's next Coutinho When the Reds spent all that money on the German, it felt like for the first time in many years, Liverpool had discovered the heir to Coutinho's throne. But Wirtz has struggled to adapt to English football. Unlike, Coutinho who settled in with ease Wirtz isn't yet catching the eye. He seems to be a little off pace, a little indecisive and just not the player we saw take the Bundesliga by storm over the course of his young career. How to unlock him remains the biggest mystery in Iraola's career. It could also determine the success of the Spaniard's time at Anfield. Things are getting better but there is no denying Wirtz could yet reach another level. Behind the scenes, Liverpool might have an alternative solution. Meet Liverpool's next Coutinho - Erik Farkas The Reds had two priorities to sort out this summer. Liverpool regard Joshua Abe and Erik Farkas as two of their biggest talents. Both attracted the interest of a host of clubs from England and abroad. But both Liverpool have now managed to secure an agreement with to sign a professional contract. Abe agreed his over the summer, and Liverpool confirmed they had agreed a deal with Farkas on Friday. This is a huge deal for the Reds. Farkas has that Coutinho quality about him. He can unlock any defence, he is blessed with a fantastic football IQ and a great vision and technical quality. Like Coutinho he's mastered those through balls with the outside of his foot. He is a pure magician and a sheer joy to watch. And thankfully Liverpool have managed to sign his services for the foreseeable future. Soon, he will be coming to join the first-team, too. Farkas already has six goals and three assists in just 553 minutes of football at academy level this season.

item.title: Palmeiras beat Vasco to move closer to the Copa do Brasil final 🇧🇷
item.description: Palmeiras beat Vasco to move closer to the Copa do Brasil final 🇧🇷 Palmeiras beat Vasco 1–0 at Nubank Park, taking an important step toward a place in the Copa do Brasil final. Maurício scored the only goal on Sunday (1) in the first leg of the semifinal. The match was marked by TWO controversies, with Vasco players protesting a penalty that was not awarded and a sending-off. What's next 🏆 The return leg between Vasco and Palmeiras will take place next Sunday (8), at 5 p.m., at São Januário. A draw will be enough for Palmeiras. Vasco need to win by at least two goals. A one-goal win for the Giant of the Hill (1–0, 2–1, 3–2...) will send the tie to penalties. The winner will face Atlético-MG or Grêmio on Sunday, December 6, at Mané Garrincha. First half 🔍 Palmeiras started better and controlled proceedings for the first 30 minutes. Giay even missed an open goal. The hosts' dominance paid off in the 24th minute. Maurício received a pass from Marlon Freitas and fired into the corner. Palmeiras eased off, and the game became feisty. The referee showed FOUR yellow cards—three of them to Vasco. Second half 🔍 The second half featured TWO controversies. Vasco players appealed for a penalty after a handball by Barboza in the box. Then, in the 77th minute, Saldívia was shown a red card, leaving Vasco down to 10 men. Did it warrant a second yellow? Watch the footage from GE and have your say! Palmeiras continued to dominate possession (61%) but, despite their numerical advantage, their final ball let them down and they could not extend their lead. But first, the Brasileirão 🇧🇷 Both clubs have fixtures in the 34th round of the Brasileirão before the semifinal return leg. Palmeiras (second with 70 points) will host Remo on Thursday (5), at 7:30 p.m., at Nubank Park. Vasco (13th with 38 points) will visit Athletico on Wednesday (4), at 7:30 p.m., at Arena da Baixada. item.title: Picture: Furious Inter ultras slam players after derby defeat
item.description: Picture: Furious Inter ultras slam players after derby defeat Inter ultras put up a banner after a 3-1 loss against Milan, criticising the players’ attitude during and after the game: ‘A derby lost without even playing. Not even the guts to say goodbye.’ Inter lost their first Serie A game of the season on Saturday, falling 3-1 to city rivals Milan. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Fans of FC Internazionale during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Although it was only Inter’s first Serie A defeat in 2026-27, their ultras didn’t like the team’s attitude or that the players left the pitch without waving to the supporters in Curva Nord. “A derby lost without even playing. Not even the guts to say goodbye,” Inter ultras wrote on a banner which they placed just outside San Siro. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Djed Spence of FC Internazionale in action during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Antonino Lagana/Getty Images) Lazio’s Sunday victory means Inter now sit second in the Serie A table, three points behind the Biancocelesti. Inter ultras blame players after 3-1 derby loss vs. Milan – Picture La delusione per il derby perso si è trasformata in una presa di posizione molto dura da parte della Curva Nord. Dopo la sconfitta contro il Milan, è comparso uno striscione dal messaggio inequivocabile: «Un derby perso senza giocare. Neanche le palle di salutare». Poche parole, ma sufficienti a raccontare il malcontento di una parte della tifoseria nerazzurra. Nel mirino non c’è soltanto il risultato, ma soprattutto l’atteggiamento mostrato dalla squadra e quanto accaduto al termine della partita. Una contestazione che riaccende il confronto tra squadra e tifosi e che testimonia quanto possa pesare una sconfitta in una partita così sentita. Il derby, ancora una volta, lascia strascichi che vanno ben oltre i novanta minuti.

item.title: New Astros GM Randy Flores helped build the Cardinals' farm system. A closer look at his draft record
item.description: JJ Wetherholt, drafted in 2024, is arguably the best first-round success story from new Astros general manager Randy Flores' time running the Cardinals' drafts. (Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) In the Houston Astros ' news release Friday announcing the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager , club owner Jim Crane's statement noted that the Astros were impressed during the interview process "with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition." Flores joined the St. Louis Cardinals' front office in August 2015 as scouting director and continued to oversee the Cardinals' amateur drafts after being promoted to assistant general manager in late 2018. His most recent title in St. Louis was assistant GM of amateur and pro acquisition. Flores' duties with St. Louis evidently went beyond just the amateur draft. He was overseeing both the Cardinals' amateur and pro scouting efforts, per the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, and The Athletic reported that Flores was involved in major-league operations including the trade deadline. Nor are the results of 11 drafts Flores led for the Cardinals a precise way to forecast how he will fare in his first crack at running a baseball operations department. Still, Crane's appraisal invites a look at St. Louis' track record of drafts and farm system strength during Flores' time there. The Astros are bringing in Flores at a pivotal juncture . Their regular-season win total has declined in four consecutive years, their core is aging and their minor-league system is ranked among the sport's thinnest by outside evaluations. For a franchise that has resisted long-term deals, strengthening the latter does appear a key part of sustaining the contending window Crane has vowed will not close during his tenure. The draft is a notoriously inexact science, and whether picks pan out can be heavily impacted afterward by player development. Scouting and player acquisition in broad terms may also extend to international signings or players added in trades or free agency. Both are caveats to this examination. Overall farm system strength may be an area to start. (Richard Rodriguez/Getty Images) In the Houston Astros ' news release Friday announcing the hiring of Randy Flores as general manager , club owner Jim Crane's statement noted that the Astros were impressed during the interview process "with Randy and his background in scouting and player acquisition." Flores joined the St. Louis Cardinals' front office in August 2015 as scouting director and continued to oversee the Cardinals' amateur drafts after being promoted to assistant general manager in late 2018. His most recent title in St. Louis was assistant GM of amateur and pro acquisition. Flores' duties with St. Louis evidently went beyond just the amateur draft. He was overseeing both the Cardinals' amateur and pro scouting efforts, per the St. Louis Post-Dispatch, and The Athletic reported that Flores was involved in major-league operations including the trade deadline. Nor are the results of 11 drafts Flores led for the Cardinals a precise way to forecast how he will fare in his first crack at running a baseball operations department. Still, Crane's appraisal invites a look at St. Louis' track record of drafts and farm system strength during Flores' time there. The Astros are bringing in Flores at a pivotal juncture . Their regular-season win total has declined in four consecutive years, their core is aging and their minor-league system is ranked among the sport's thinnest by outside evaluations. For a franchise that has resisted long-term deals, strengthening the latter does appear a key part of sustaining the contending window Crane has vowed will not close during his tenure. The draft is a notoriously inexact science, and whether picks pan out can be heavily impacted afterward by player development. Scouting and player acquisition in broad terms may also extend to international signings or players added in trades or free agency. Both are caveats to this examination. Overall farm system strength may be an area to start. From 2016 through 2023, the Cardinals' system ranked between ninth and 14th out of 30 teams in Baseball America's preseason rankings in each year except one. It then dipped to 20th in 2024 and ranked 18th in 2025. Starting in 2025, the Cardinals entered a kind of rebuild, reducing major-league payroll and reportedly investing more in player development and technology. They reduced payroll further in 2026, largely by trading away veterans on larger contracts before the season. St. Louis' farm system climbed to No. 2 in the Baseball America preseason rankings this year, with its highest-rated prospects mainly a mix of players acquired in those trades last offseason and selections from its recent drafts. From 2016-23, their first eight drafts under Flores, the Cardinals never picked higher than No. 18. They forfeited their top two picks in 2017 , as well, as a punishment for former scouting director Chris Correa illegally accessing the Astros' computer database . Related or not, many of the Cardinals' draft successes to this point under Flores stemmed from middle rounds. St. Louis made 14 first-round selections from 2016-26. Of those, shortstop JJ Wetherholt, who was taken with the No. 7 overall pick in 2024 and debuted in 2026, has already accrued the most wins above replacement, per Baseball Reference, with 4.5 bWAR. That reflects some early misses. Jordan Walker, the Cardinals' first-round pick in 2020, made the All-Star team in a breakout 2026 season, though, illustrating how draft evaluations may evolve with time. The shortened 2020 draft could prove particularly fruitful for St. Louis, as the second round yielded Masyn Winn, the Kingwood High school alumnus and its current shortstop, and Alec Burleson, who led the majors in RBIs this season. In 2016, the Cardinals drafted pitcher Zac Gallen in the third round and infielder Tommy Edman in the sixth. Edman has accrued 20.7 bWAR in the majors, to this point the most of any player drafted under Flores. Gallen, who was traded as a minor-leaguer in a package for slugger Marcell Ozuna, is second at 19 bWAR, all accrued with other clubs. In 2018, the Cardinals selected Brendan Donovan in the seventh round and Lars Nootbaar in the eighth. Donovan became an All-Star with St. Louis and was among the players traded last winter, garnering the Cardinals a haul of prospects and draft picks. Nootbaar became part of the Cardinals' outfield and was their longest-tenured position player when he was traded at this year's deadline. With no playoff appearances since 2022, the Cardinals drafted seventh overall in 2024, fifth overall in 2025 - selecting pitcher Liam Doyle - and five times in the first two rounds in 2026. Wetherholt, their first-rounder in 2024, is the only player from those three classes who has played in the majors at this point, so a full appraisal of later drafts under Flores won't be apparent for years. In total, players drafted by the Cardinals from 2016-24 have combined for 112.7 bWAR in the majors. As a comparison, players drafted by the Astros in that same stretch have accrued 49.1 bWAR. The latter number reflects Houston's issues in the draft over the past decade. The Astros forfeited their top two picks in 2020 and '21 as punishment for the franchise's sign-stealing scandal , but other early selections have gone unrealized. Since 2016, players drafted in the first round by the Astros have totaled minus-1.1 bWAR in the majors, while their second-round picks have combined for minus-2.7 bWAR. Baseball America ranked them 25th at midseason, while MLB Pipeline and ESPN both had their system at 29th. Drafts and scouting may no longer be Flores' primary responsibility in his new role as Houston's general manager. But one of his challenges will be to replenish a poorly rated farm system while also upholding Crane's mandate that the Astros remain a perennial playoff team. What ideas or lessons from a decade overseeing scouting in St. Louis he will bring to bear on that task remains to be seen. Baker Mayfield did not complete a pass, yet the Buccaneers didn’t care because they ran for 300 yards. The Falcons had Bijan Robinson, but somehow that didn’t matter because the Falcons got down after throwing too much and then started throwing nonstop late. The Falcons were within striking distance—or at least not dead—all day, but yet could not turn in a single point. There is nothing that can be said about the caliber of performance the Falcons put on the field today that is positive, and aside from a handful of strong individual performances, Atlanta was humiliated and humbled by their rival. Now 3-5, the Falcons are back down with the Buccaneers and the division is a muddle, and Atlanta’s highs are matched by their lows as they continue to be defined by inconsistency and utterly baffling performances after stunningly good ones. item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well).
